claim: Luca: treat the market's correlations as a curved space, as general relativity treats gravity; the curvature of that space should tell you where aggregates (the market, funds, groups) go next.

version_tested.what: Each month, the 500 most-traded US stocks; edges join the 5% most-correlated pairs over 63 days (6,237 edges); edge length sqrt(2(1 - rho)). Ollivier-Ricci curvature (optimal transport between neighbourhoods) and Forman curvature (degrees and triangles), averaged over edges.
version_tested.tests: B1 (what it is made of), B2 (does it improve forecasts of SPY next month?), B3 (a timing rule)

version_tested.what: Covariance matrices of the same 500 stocks over 21, 63 and 252 days, shrunk; combined either as plain matrices (Euclidean) or in matrix-log coordinates (log-Euclidean); judged by the realized risk of the minimum-variance portfolio each builds.
(market return, volatility, average correlation) with a learned metric; do markets follow its geodesics?
version_tested.tests: B4: deferred by the plan, not run

verdict.short: No: curvature adds nothing to forecasts of the market's direction or its risk, a curvature timing rule matched random timing, and the curved-space covariance representation did not beat the flat one.

key_numbers.name: B2 direction, Clark-West t
key_numbers.meaning: Adding Ollivier curvature to the forecast of SPY's next-month excess return, beyond volatility, average correlation, the absorption ratio and plain graph statistics, 2008-2019. Needed t >= 3.

key_numbers.name: B2 risk, Clark-West t
key_numbers.meaning: The same for SPY's next-month volatility: the forecast got slightly worse with curvature.

key_numbers.name: Curvature explained by plain graph statistics, R^2
key_numbers.meaning: How much of the monthly Ollivier series four counting statistics (degree concentration, triangles, edge correlation, largest component) reproduce. Forman: exactly 1.

key_numbers.name: B3 timing rule minus random timing, points a year
key_numbers.meaning: Holding 100% SPY in calm-curvature months and 50% otherwise, 2005-04..2025-06, against 10,000 random orders of the same months (p 0.61). After 5 bps costs, -3.1 points a year against SPY.

key_numbers.name: B5 Euclidean minus log-Euclidean risk, t
key_numbers.meaning: Paired monthly difference in the minimum-variance portfolio's realized variance, 2006-2019; positive would favour the log-Euclidean (matrix-log) representation.

key_numbers.name: Odd vs even days, curvature correlation
key_numbers.meaning: Ollivier curvature computed from a window's odd days against its even days, across months. The halves agree only moderately, so much of the monthly movement is estimation noise.

chart_curvature_vs_drawdown.description: Monthly mean Ollivier-Ricci curvature of the 5% graph (and its z-score against the previous 60 month-ends), against SPY's drawdown from its running peak. The plan reads high Ollivier as the crisis side (Sandhu et al.).
chart_curvature_vs_drawdown.base_rate_note: A z-score above +1 occurs in 15% of months and at least once in 71% of all 13-month spans, so a spike in the year before a peak is what chance gives.

chart_forecast_skill.description: Cumulative out-of-sample squared-error gain from adding Ollivier curvature (model 3 vs model 2), by month; rising means curvature helps. Also the Clark-West t of each comparison (bar 3).

labels.m2->m3: Ollivier beyond graph statistics (the key test)
labels.m1->m_samal: Samal et al.'s Forman vs baseline

chart_b3_rule.description: Growth of $1 at 5 bps costs, bought at the close after each month-end decision, cash at the T-bill; and the distribution of 10,000 random timings with the same months at 100% and 50%.

chart_b5_volatility.description: Annualized realized volatility of the capped minimum-variance portfolio built from each covariance forecast, by period. Euclidean and log-Euclidean share windows, grid, shrinkage and weight choice; only the representation differs. LW-252 is the existing MV-LW estimator; the affine step is B A^-1 B (reported only).

what_results_can_and_cant_show: B2 direction is the closest test of Luca's geometric claim. It failed: curvature did not improve the forecast of SPY's next-month return beyond volatility, average correlation, the absorption ratio and plain graph statistics.

B2 risk failed too: Ollivier curvature added nothing to the forecast of next-month volatility beyond the same inputs. Forman curvature (degrees and triangles) improved the risk forecast over the baseline at t 2.7 in 2008-2019, below the bar of 3, and not in 2020-2025 (t -0.8).

B3's rule is one allocation rule; it matched random timing at the same exposure. Its smaller drawdown than SPY (31% against 55%) is matched by the plain volatility threshold (31%) and beaten by volatility-managed SPY (23%).
B5 is about representing covariances, not about market curvature: the log-Euclidean metric is flat. It did not beat the Euclidean combination.

Curvature here is mostly simpler statistics renamed: four counting statistics explain 92% of the Ollivier series and 100% of Forman, and rebuilding returns from market and sector factors alone gives slightly more Ollivier curvature than the real data (0.161 against 0.149).
Much of a month's curvature is estimation noise: computed from a window's odd days and its even days, the two series correlate 0.53 across months.
Twenty years hold only a handful of large drawdowns; curvature spikes before peaks occur at the rate chance gives.
The stock data has only companies still listed, so crisis-period results may be biased.
No result here could show that relativity's equations, or any law like them, govern markets; no field equation links money to this curvature.
Forward confirmation on closes after 2026-10-19 is pending; the 16 unseen months were already read by about 65 experiments.
